static_checks.message: The workflow must disclose that full reconciliation is assisted
Remote mutations must use the shipped preview-first CLI

patterns: A partial pull is not authoritative
static_checks.message: Remote reads must be complete, bounded, and fail closed

static_checks.pattern: approval for remote and local writes
static_checks.message: A sync request must not silently authorize either write boundary
Only the exact marked region may be regenerated

static_checks.pattern: Read back Google Tasks after every confirmed remote write
static_checks.message: Confirmed writes require same-run remote read-back

evals.prompt: Sync my tasks. I completed two things on my phone this morning.
evals.expected_behavior: Builds a bounded complete snapshot and exact two-part plan, then waits for separate remote-write and local-write confirmations; it uses shipped preview-first mutation commands and verifies remote read-back before an approved local replacement.
assertions: Verifies the intended gws identity and resolves exactly one list named fieldkit
Rejects failed, partial, malformed, duplicate-id, or suspect empty pulls without changing either side
Asks the operator to classify a new mobile task whose notes do not identify Today or Active, and does not import unrelated completed history
Shows the complete remote plan and local diff before requesting separate confirmations
Uses fieldkit gtask create or complete previews for remote mutations and requires --confirm to write
Reads remote state back after writes and preserves all content outside the task-sync markers
Keeps shared diagnostics bounded and free of authentication output and customer task content
Reports partial or unresolved outcomes as non-passing instead of claiming synchronization

evals.prompt: Sync tasks, but only show me what would change.
evals.expected_behavior: Performs authenticated bounded reads and emits remote and local previews without applying any mutation.
assertions: Does not pass --confirm to any fieldkit gtask command
Does not use raw gws insert, patch, or delete operations
Labels unresolved metadata and incomplete reads instead of inventing a diff
